title: Routing: burst-aware route selection (baseline → burst pool → fallback) + integration tests
author: Elena Popov
commits: routing: add RoutePlan with baseline/burst/fallback candidates
routing: wire burst eligibility + pool health gates into planner
routing: propagate burst decision reason into response headers/log context
tests: add integration cases for baseline->burst and burst-denied behavior
docs(internal): update runbook notes for routing debug fields
body:
Summary: This adds burst-aware routing for Redwood Dedicated tenants: we now attempt baseline dedicated capacity first, then (optionally) route to a controlled burst pool when baseline is saturated, and finally apply fallback rules (alternate region/model variant) only when explicitly permitted by tenant policy. Includes integration tests that simulate baseline saturation, burst eligibility/denial, and burst pool health transitions.

Context: Dedicated Burst (ENG-4824) needs routing semantics that are deterministic and explainable. The routing layer must not accidentally spill Dedicated traffic into shared pools unless (a) the tenant is enabled for burst, (b) policy grants the request, and (c) the target burst pool is healthy and within routing safety thresholds.

What changed (high-level): - Added a RoutePlan abstraction that builds an ordered list of route candidates with attached constraints and reason codes. - Implemented burst-aware candidate generation: baseline candidate is always first; burst candidates are inserted only when tenant burst is enabled AND policy returns allow=true AND the burst pool health gate is open. - Implemented fallback semantics: if burst is denied, we do not attempt burst pools; we either return a capacity error immediately or (if tenant allows fallback) try a configured fallback model/region. - Added reason codes and debug fields to logs and response headers for traceability (safe subset; no internal pool IDs are exposed).

Routing algorithm (v1): 1) Baseline: Attempt routing to the tenant's baseline Dedicated pool (same region) using existing SLO-aware scoring. 2) Burst candidate insertion (only when baseline cannot admit): If baseline admission fails with a capacity-related reason (queue full / no allocatable slots / saturation), call Burst Policy Service (cached) for {tenant, region, model} eligibility. If allowed, add one or more burst pool candidates in the same region/GPU family, ordered by pool health score. 3) Fallback: If burst is not allowed OR all burst candidates are closed by health gate, apply fallback rules: - If tenant has allow_fallback_region=true, try the tenant's configured fallback region(s) for baseline first, then burst (same gating rules). - If tenant has allow_fallback_model=true, try the configured compatible model variant (e.g., instruct vs base) only within the same privacy/isolation class. Otherwise return an error to the client.

Important constraints: - Noisy-neighbor protections: routing never selects a burst pool without a positive policy decision. - Determinism: route planning is now a pure function of (request, tenant config snapshot, policy decision, pool health snapshot). No randomization in candidate ordering. - Safety: we do not fall back across regions by default; it is opt-in per tenant.

Integration tests: Added routing integration tests that spin up a fake policy service + fake fleet health provider and validate end-to-end handler behavior (including headers). Key cases: - baseline_ok_does_not_call_policy: if baseline admits, we never query burst policy. - baseline_saturated_burst_allowed_routes_to_burst: baseline admission fails with CapacityShed → policy allow → selected route is burst. - baseline_saturated_burst_denied_returns_capacity_error: policy deny with reason=TENANT_LIMIT → no burst attempt → returns 429-like capacity response (internal code; external semantics to be finalized in follow-up). - burst_pool_gate_closed_falls_back_when_allowed: policy allow but pool gate closed due to saturation → fallback region candidate selected only if tenant allows. - fallback_not_allowed_returns_error: baseline saturated + burst denied + fallback disabled → return capacity error with reason code.

Telemetry / debugging: - Added structured fields: route.selected_tier=(baseline|burst|fallback), route.burst_decision=(allow|deny|skipped), route.deny_reason_code, route.fallback_applied=(true|false). - Response headers (debug mode / internal clients only for now): x-redwood-route-tier, x-redwood-burst (allow|deny|skipped), x-redwood-burst-reason (sanitized enum).

Known gaps / follow-ups: - External error semantics (429 vs 503) and retry guidance will be refined (see discussion; follow-up tracked separately). - We intentionally avoid exposing pool identifiers; SREs can correlate via trace IDs + internal logs.

Review notes / conversation (condensed): - Mina Haddad: Please ensure we never call policy service on the hot path if baseline admits; also require capacity-failure-only trigger for policy call. Elena: Updated planner to short-circuit on baseline success and only evaluate burst on capacity-related admit failures; added test baseline_ok_does_not_call_policy. - Ravi Menon: Fallback should not implicitly cross region; must be explicit per tenant config. Elena: Added config gates allow_fallback_region/allow_fallback_model (default false) and validated in planner; updated fixtures. - Peter Holtz: Need clearer reason codes for why burst was not attempted (skipped vs denied vs gate closed). Elena: Split burst_decision into skipped/deny/allow and added gate_closed as separate pool_health outcome; logs now include both. - Ethan Park: Policy client caching: ensure we use the policy snapshot TTL and fail closed on policy errors. Elena: Implemented TTL caching keyed by (tenant, region, model) with 2s default; on policy error we mark burst_decision=skipped and do not attempt burst.

CI / rollout: - Initial CI run failed on integration test flake due to fixture ordering; fixed by making fixture load deterministic and increasing readiness wait for fake policy server. - Merged after green integration + e2e-smoke.

Release notes (internal): Adds burst-aware routing behavior behind feature flag routing.burst_enabled. No customer-visible behavior change unless tenant is enabled for Dedicated Burst beta.

Refs: Linear ENG-4824. Related: control-plane policy plumbing and admission headers will follow in adjacent PRs; this PR focuses on routing decision and test coverage.
